summary: Design risk-linked health monitoring, manage confidential records, and report trends. Explore this five-day practical occupational health course.
lede: Occupational health surveillance connects workplace exposures with suitable worker health checks and follow-up for occupational health nurses, hygienists, physicians, and safety professionals. The course covers prioritizing exposure risks, designing risk-linked protocols, and handling confidential health records. Learners also practice tracking referrals, interpreting aggregated trends, and using Excel registers and dashboards to review preventive controls.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate workplace health checks, interpret occupational exposure information, or use health findings to improve preventive controls. It suits intermediate learners with experience in occupational health, safety, hygiene, or workforce health services.
modules: Health Trend Analysis and Digital Reporting
prerequisites: Prior experience in occupational health, occupational safety, industrial hygiene, workforce health, or a closely related workplace role is recommended. You should be familiar with basic hazard identification and workplace risk assessment. No coding is required; exercises use supplied materials and an Excel-based dataset.
